answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring a tundra-tier identity to lock a bond for 24 epochs before earning full rewards. Each round, two randomly selected independent peers audit a distinct task, and a failed audit burns 20 percent of the bond. A haven reputation score rises only after 6 consecutive accepted rounds, while a velvet fingerprint ledger detects correlated outputs across accounts. Every extra fake identity therefore adds capital, audit work, and a long delay, while signed task records make verification reproducible.
